participants: Andrew Jin / Andrew Musial (closer, Primal Instinct)
summary: Monday meeting opening with the announcement that Kyla Louie has also left the team on performance grounds, leaving Kim as the sole setter with full lead flow. Chris announces that ads are being switched back on, the new VSL script is finished and cold traffic will follow, and states a deliberate change of target profile away from good-to-great prospects toward men 20-30 pounds overweight and former athletes carrying injuries. Andrew reports no units - the EJ Hernandez deposit failed that morning - and is out from Wednesday. Ben and Chris discuss financing arithmetic on the $6,000 programme. The remainder is a long training block on the transition from pitch to price drop, run as a manager demonstration and then two rep roleplays, covering the 1-10 temperature check, the certainty tie-down, the finances double tie-down and the custom-payment-plan opener, which Chris dictates word for word.
notable: Explicit reversal of the stated ICP: 'We want to get away from the good to great guys, because they just haven't really... they usually look at it, even if they have the money, and say, I don't really feel like I need to spend 6k to get 5 pounds off my body.' New target is men 20-30 pounds overweight and injured former athletes. This is the opposite of what prospects are told on live calls.

Financing arithmetic stated openly: 12 months through the financing partner brings the $6,000 programme to roughly $7,800, or $650 a month, and Chris instructs reps to anchor on the monthly figure and away from the total. Flagged separately.
Chris ranks the three most important tie-downs: certainty that the programme will get the result, then 'if we can solve the objection you're in right now', then commitment.

Chris explicitly rejects guilt and fear selling as a matter of personal style - 'I don't lead with guilt... I don't want somebody to like close because they're afraid' - which sits directly against the Manny complaint recorded on 06/10 and the pressure applied on the EJ Hernandez call the same morning.

Chris instructs reps to take the card and enter it themselves rather than sending a payment link - 'Nope. Not good. Don't want to do that' - because links invite delay. Both closers had been sending links.

Chris states he does not financially qualify B2C fitness prospects at all - 'in fitness, to be honest with you, most of the time I just throw that out' - and prefers to pitch first and use the prospect's certainty to overcome a spouse rather than involve them, taking a deposit and booking a follow-up.
Two departures inside eight days (Harry Edmonds 06/10, Kyla Louie 06/15) plus ads off and then back on means the setter mix, closer coverage and lead source all shift inside this batch window.
A closed client in Spain (Jorge) had emergency appendix surgery over the weekend with payment still outstanding; the discussion turned to whether he would still close.
